summary: Sumanapala Galmangoda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) and as Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2012).

Sumathi Ramaswamy is an Indologist and historian. She studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania, where she held a post (~1993-1995) before teaching history at the University of Michigan (~2000-2007).

Sumi Lee is a Buddhist studies scholar. She completed an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and earned her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles under Robert E. Buswell Jr. (attested 2014).

Sumitra Mangesh Katre was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from the University of London. He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1942-1971), and the University of Texas at Austin (1971-1976).

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Juhyung Rhi and studied under Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.

Sung Bae Park is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed his doctoral studies under Lewis Lancaster. He taught at Dongguk University (~1970-1973), held a post at Stony Brook University (1977), and founded the International Association for Wonhyo Studies.

Sungdoo Ahn is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He served as Director of Geumgang University and as Professor at Seoul National University (attested 2013).
Sungtaek Cho is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at Stony Brook University and at Korea University, where he served as Director (attested 2012-2013).
Sunhee Kim completed a Doctor of Philosophy in Performance Practice at the University of Exeter under the supervision of Phillip Zarrilli.

Suniti Kumar Chatterji was an Indian linguist and Indologist. Educated at Scottish Church College, Presidency University, Calcutta, London, and Paris, he long served as professor at the University of Calcutta and later as National Professor in Humanities (~1965-1977).

Surama Dasgupta was an Indologist and philosopher who earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and a PhD from the University of Cambridge, studying under Surendranath Dasgupta. She served as Reader in Philosophy at the University of Lucknow (~1950-1968).
Surendra Man Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Tribhuvan University under the supervision of Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya and co-supervision of Ranjana Bajracharya.

Surendranath Dasgupta was an Indian philosopher and Indologist who earned doctorates from Calcutta and Cambridge. He held professorships at Chittagong College, Presidency College, and Calcutta, and served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1931-1942).
Surendranath Sen was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Calcutta (~1917-1939) and the University of Delhi (~1950-1953).

Surya Kumar Bhuyan was an Indologist and historian who studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, Calcutta, and SOAS. He served as Principal of Cotton University (1918) and later as Vice Chancellor of Gauhati University (~1957-1960).

Susan Andrews is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. She earned her PhD at Columbia University, where she studied under her doctoral supervisor Chün-fang Yü, as well as Bernard Faure, D. Max Moerman, and others.

Susan J. Rosenfield is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Harvard University in 2004. Her teachers included Stephanie W. Jamison, George L. Hart, Kausalya Hart, Shaligram Shukla, Saudamani Deshmukh, James W. Benson, and Thomas Burke.
Susan L. Beningson is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University (attested 2009) under the supervision of Robert E. Harrist, Jr.
Susan L. Huntington is a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. She spent her career at Ohio State University (~1971-2011), where she was Professor from ~1984 to 2010.

Susan Naquin is a historian of China and religious studies scholar. She earned her BA at Stanford and MA and PhD at Yale, before teaching at the University of Pennsylvania (1977-1988) and serving as Professor at Princeton University (1993-2013).
